sample.universe: All employees of the Danish textile and clothing sector in 1999 aged 17-57 as of 1999 (quota experiment sample, N = 10,487); for the economy-wide analysis, the 1999 private-sector cohort of workers (N = 900,329)
sample.unit_of_observation: worker x period observation (the annual worker-level records are aggregated into a pre-shock and a post-shock period)
selection_rules: employed in the textile and clothing sector in Denmark as of 1999
aged between 17 and 57 years as of 1999
treatment defined by the 1999 employer's revenue share of CN-8 goods subject to the MFA quota removal for China; workers at firms with a zero share form the control group
sub-samples defined by the worker's occupational wage group as of 1999 (mid-wage: N = 13,934 observations; high-wage: N = 4294; low-wage: N = 2496)
non-agricultural occupations only; military and agricultural occupations are not ranked (ISCO 92 excluded)
for the task analysis, workers whose 1999 four-digit occupation can be matched to the relevant O*NET task variable (estimation N varies between 18,428 and 20,728)
sample.period: 1999-2009 (annual register data back to 1990 used for the falsification tests)
sample.n_observations: 20,974 worker-period observations in the main specification (Table 3)
sample.n_individuals: 10,487 textile and clothing workers; 900,329 workers in the economy-wide sample

construction_notes: Occupations are classified into high-, mid- and low-wage groups on the basis of the median hourly wage paid in a full-time occupation in Denmark in 1999 (Table 1); wages are expressed in log 2000 Danish Kroner
Hourly wages are calculated among workers with full-time jobs employed continuously with at least one year of tenure; employment shares exclude military, agriculture and fishery occupations

Exposure99ik = sum over quota products p of the firm's 1999 per-product revenue divided by the firm's total 1999 revenue; all active MFA quotas imposed on China are considered, including those of the 2005 liberalization phase
Post_s is an indicator for the post-liberalization period 2002-2009
Annual data are aggregated into pre- and post-shock periods to address the serial correlation concerns of Bertrand et al. (2004)
MIDeis, HIGHeis, LOWeis, UEeis and OUTeis are mutually exclusive but not exhaustive, since military and agricultural occupations are not ranked
The primary labour-market position of an individual in a given year is determined by Statistics Denmark on the basis of the individual's position as of November of that year
In the economy-wide analysis MIDei is the sum of all years from 2000 to 2009 in which worker i held a primary job in mid-wage occupations, ranging from 0 to 10
Alternative outcome measures used in robustness checks: full-time years of employment, total hours worked, and cumulative earnings in each occupation group (Online Appendix Table B-6)
O*NET task variables are continuous measures of the intensity of a task in a given four-digit ISCO occupation, matched on the worker's 1999 occupation

claims.statement: Exposure to rising Chinese import competition due to the MFA quota removals reduced the number of years textile workers spent in mid-wage occupations over 2002-2009.

treatment.label: Import Competition (ImpComp = Exposure99ik x Posts), continuous exposure

register_source.value: Firm-product level production database (VARES) matched to CN-8 quota products, merged to workers via IDA

definition.value: Difference-in-differences term: the 1999 revenue share of the worker's employer k from eight-digit CN goods that were subject to removal of MFA import quotas for China (Exposure99ik = sum of per-product revenue from quota products divided by the firm's total 1999 revenue), interacted with an indicator for the post-liberalization period 2002-2009. Workers at firms with a zero revenue share are the control group; workers at firms with positive shares are treated at varying levels

timing.value: Exposure fixed at its 1999 (pre-shock) value; the quota removals take effect in January 2002 after China's WTO entry in December 2001, so Posts = 1 for 2002-2009

outcome.label: Years of employment in mid-wage occupations (MIDeis)

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), Statistics Denmark

definition.value: Number of years in period s in which worker i's primary labour-market position is employment in a mid-wage occupation (clerks/office workers, craft and related trade workers, plant and machine operators and assemblers), where occupations are grouped by the 1999 median hourly wage of one-digit ISCO occupations

timing.value: Labour-market status measured as of November of each year; years are cumulated within the pre-shock period and within the post-shock period 2002-2009 (two-period aggregation of the annual data)

units.value: years of employment in the period, per unit of exposure (the 1999 revenue share of quota products, 0-1)

magnitude.interpretation: Comparing the 75th and 25th percentile of exposure (a difference of 0.284), import competition causes 1.292 x 0.284 = 0.367 of a year, or 4.4 months, less mid-wage employment over the eight post-shock years, a 13% reduction relative to the control group's 2.8 years

identification.source_of_variation: EU-wide dismantling of Multi-Fibre Arrangement import quotas on Chinese textile and clothing products following China's WTO entry (December 2001), which raised import competition for Danish textile firms in proportion to their 1999 revenue share of quota-protected CN-8 products; workers at firms with zero such revenue are controls

key_assumptions.assumption: In the absence of the quota removal, exposed and non-exposed textile workers would have followed parallel trends in their labour-market outcomes
key_assumptions.supported_by: Placebo/falsification difference-in-differences for 1990-1999 (pre-period 1990-94, post-period 1995-99) using the same treatment definition finds all estimates close to zero and insignificant (Online Appendix Tables B-3 and B-4); randomly assigning firms' exposure centres coefficients on zero (Table B-5)

formal.as_written: α1 in Eq. (1) is the linear difference-in-differences estimator

key_assumptions.assumption: The removal of the MFA import quotas on China is exogenous to Danish textile firms and their workers: neither Denmark nor China negotiated the creation or removal of the quotas, which were set at the EU level and triggered by China's WTO accession
key_assumptions.supported_by: Institutional argument about EU-level negotiation and China's WTO entry in December 2001

evidence.annotation: Notes: Shown are difference-in-differences coefﬁcients from estimating Eq. (1) with varying sample period ending from 2002 to 2009. Sample is all high-wage textile workers as of the initial year 1999. The number of observations in every regression is N = 4294. Dependent variables are given in the ﬁgure legend.
